staged_source_snapshot.description: This host-side `_work` checkout is the staged vulnerable source snapshot for the sample. The live ARVO workspace container exposes the same tree at `/src/freeradius-server`; Stage 02 inspected the source through that live mount and then confirmed line-exactness against this host path.

classification.classification_note: ASan reports a 1-byte global-buffer-overflow read in `fr_is_base16_nstd`, but the bug-triggering logic is earlier in TACACS argument decoding: raw OCTETS bytes from the packet are misrouted into the base16 parser instead of being copied verbatim.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42502974 (freeradius-server): Global-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target fuzzer_tacacs [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42502974
bug_description.normalized: The staged 80-byte witness is accepted by `fr_tacacs_decode()` as an unencrypted TACACS+ authorization response: header bytes `c0 02 20 ff 20 20 20 20 00 00 00 44` mean version `0xc0`, type `FR_TAC_PLUS_AUTHOR`, even `seq_no=0x20` (so `packet_is_author_response(pkt)` is true), flags `0xff` with `FR_TAC_PLUS_UNENCRYPTED_FLAG` set (so line 306 skips decryption), and body length `0x44`. The response body carries `arg_cnt=9`, `server_msg_len=1`, `data_len=9`, arg lengths `[0,2,0,0,0,0,0,0,41]`, and a final 41-byte argument `DATa*0x` + 9x`0x20` + `0xff 0xff` + 23x`0x20`. `tacacs_decode_args()` copies that argument, splits it at `*`, and resolves the mixed-case name `DATa` case-insensitively to the TACACS `Data` attribute, whose dictionary type is `FR_TYPE_OCTETS`. Vulnerable line 162 then always calls `fr_pair_value_from_str()` on the raw value even for OCTETS and STRING attributes. Because the 36-byte value is `0x` + 9x`0x20` + `0xff 0xff` + 23x`0x20`, `fr_value_box_from_str()` takes its OCTETS hex-decode path instead of the verbatim-copy path, strips the prefix, and asks `fr_base16_decode_nstd()` to parse a 34-byte payload whose fifth pair is `0x20 0xff`. `fr_base16_decode_nstd()` evaluates both `a = fr_is_base16_nstd(p[0], alphabet)` and `b = fr_is_base16_nstd(p[1], alphabet)` before the `if (!a || !b)` block, so line 155 calls `fr_is_base16_nstd()` on that second byte `0xff`. The helper casts `0xff` to index 255 and reads `fr_base16_alphabet_decode_mc[255]`; the table is declared as `fr_base16_alphabet_decode_mc[UINT8_MAX]`, so its valid indices are only 0 through 254. That one-byte read past the static table produces the saved AddressSanitizer global-buffer-overflow at the staged expression `src/lib/util/base16.h:53` (reported by ASan through the include alias `src/freeradius-devel/util/base16.h:53`). The staged patch fixes the TACACS-side missing obligation by copying OCTETS and STRING argument values verbatim in `tacacs_decode_args()` instead of routing them through the generic string parser.

source.description: First non-harness project statement on the vulnerable path that materializes the attacker-controlled TACACS argument bytes into parser-owned storage.
source.value_from: The saved `poc` is an 80-byte unencrypted TACACS authorization response. Its body declares `arg_cnt=9`, `server_msg_len=1`, `data_len=9`, and arg lengths `[0,2,0,0,0,0,0,0,41]`, so on the final `i=8` iteration this copy reads the ninth 41-byte argument bytes `DATa*0x` + 9x`0x20` + `0xff 0xff` + 23x`0x20` from the witness into `buffer`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: ASan sink. The fifth decode pair's second byte `0xff` from the TACACS argument is cast to index 255 and used to read the mixed-case base16 decode table.
sink.note: The staged checkout contains this expression at `src/lib/util/base16.h:53`; the saved sanitizer trace reports the same inline header through the include alias `src/freeradius-devel/util/base16.h:53:9`, and ASan states the address is `0 bytes to the right of global variable 'fr_base16_alphabet_decode_mc' ... of size 255`.

root_cause.code: if (fr_pair_value_from_str(vp, (char const *) value, arg_end - value, 0, true) < 0) {
root_cause.description: This call sends recognized TACACS argument values through the generic string-to-value parser even when the dictionary attribute is OCTETS or STRING. For the `Data` attribute, that wrongly interprets raw packet bytes as textual data.
root_cause.note: The staged patch inserts exact `da->type == FR_TYPE_OCTETS` and `da->type == FR_TYPE_STRING` special-cases before this line and copies those values verbatim, so the buggy generic parse is skipped for this witness.

tainted_value_origin.description: This separator scan turns the copied argument into a mixed-case attribute name and the exact raw value that later reaches the base16 helper.
tainted_value_origin.note: On the witness, the separator is `*` after the four name bytes `DATa`, so `buffer` becomes `DATa` and `value .. arg_end` becomes the exact 36-byte payload `0x` + 9x`0x20` + `0xff 0xff` + 23x`0x20`.

parser_admitted.code:
if (tacacs_decode_args(ctx, cursor, attr_tacacs_argument_list,
			pkt->author.res.arg_cnt, BODY(author.res), &p, end) < 0) goto fail;
parser_admitted.description: The witness header selects the authorization-response parser (`pkt->hdr.type == FR_TAC_PLUS_AUTHOR` and even `seq_no=0x20`), flags `0xff` keep the body unencrypted, and `ARG_COUNT_CHECK` accepts the nine argument-length bytes, so control reaches `tacacs_decode_args()` on the response arguments.

evidence_limitations: `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to false. `trace_feedback.json` requested only source-grounded repairs, so Stage 02 did not instrument; the chain is closed entirely from the staged vulnerable source, patch hunk, saved ASan trace, reproduction report, and direct inspection of the saved `poc` bytes.

Stage 02 does not execute the fixed tree, so `sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves` remains false even though the staged patch directly adds the missing OCTETS/STRING special-case in `tacacs_decode_args()`.

fine_trace.note: Source. The witness reaches the final `i=8` argument after `fr_tacacs_decode()` has already accepted an unencrypted authorization-response body with arg lengths `[0,2,0,0,0,0,0,0,41]`. This copy materializes that ninth 41-byte argument as `DATa*0x` + 9x`0x20` + `0xff 0xff` + 23x`0x20`.

Scanning the copied argument finds `*` after the first four bytes. The parser therefore terminates the name as `DATa` and sets `value .. arg_end` to the exact 36-byte raw payload `0x` + 9x`0x20` + `0xff 0xff` + 23x`0x20` that later reaches the OCTETS parser.

Dictionary lookup resolves the mixed-case name `DATa` to TACACS attribute `Data`, because dictionary name comparison is case-insensitive (`strcasecmp` in `dict_attr_name_cmp`). TACACS base.c declares `Data` as `FR_TYPE_OCTETS`, so the upcoming value parse will use OCTETS conversion rules instead of the raw `Argument-List` string fallback.

fine_trace.code: if (fr_pair_value_from_str(vp, (char const *) value, arg_end - value, 0, true) < 0) {
fine_trace.note: Root cause. With step 3's `Data` attribute, `da->type` is `FR_TYPE_OCTETS`, yet this line still routes the 36 raw bytes through the generic string parser. The staged fix adds missing OCTETS/STRING special-cases here so those values are copied verbatim instead of parsed.

The generic OCTETS parser checks only for a leading `0x`. Here `dst_type == FR_TYPE_OCTETS`, `len == 36`, and the first two bytes are exactly `0x`, so the verbatim-copy branch is not taken and execution commits to hex decoding the remaining bytes.
After consuming the `0x` prefix, the would-be hex payload length becomes 34 bytes: 9x`0x20`, then `0xff 0xff`, then 23x`0x20`.

The only guard before decoding is the even-length test, and it passes because `len == 34`. The function therefore allocates `ret == 17` output bytes and calls `fr_base16_decode()` on the full 34-byte payload even though it contains non-hex raw bytes.

fine_trace.code:
a = fr_is_base16_nstd(p[0], alphabet);
b = fr_is_base16_nstd(p[1], alphabet);
fine_trace.note: The decode loop consumes the 34-byte payload two bytes at a time. Because the payload starts with 9 spaces, the first four pairs are `0x20 0x20` and the fifth pair is `0x20 0xff`. Lines 154-155 evaluate both `a = fr_is_base16_nstd(p[0], alphabet)` and `b = fr_is_base16_nstd(p[1], alphabet)` before line 156 can test `if (!a || !b)`, so the second call receives `p[1] == 0xff` and reaches the sink.

Sink. Here `c` is step 8's `p[1] == 0xff` from the fifth pair `0x20 0xff`, so `(uint8_t)c` is 255. The mixed-case decode table was declared as `fr_base16_alphabet_decode_mc[UINT8_MAX]` in base16.c, which gives only 255 entries with valid indices 0..254. Reading `alphabet[255]` therefore performs the 1-byte global over-read reported by ASan.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Not applicable: this sample is a global-buffer-overflow read from a static decode table, and the saved ASan report has no allocation/free context.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: The saved ASan stack `fr_is_base16_nstd -> fr_base16_decode_nstd -> fr_value_box_from_str -> fr_pair_value_from_str -> tacacs_decode_args -> fr_tacacs_decode -> fr_tacacs_decode_proto` matches fine-trace steps 4-9. Fine-trace step 9 is anchored to the staged header path `src/lib/util/base16.h:53`, while ASan frame 0 names the same inline expression through the build include alias `src/freeradius-devel/util/base16.h:53`.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: The witness-controlled ninth TACACS argument is `DATa*0x` + 9x`0x20` + `0xff 0xff` + 23x`0x20` at step 1, step 2 turns its suffix into the exact 36-byte raw value, step 3 resolves `DATa` to OCTETS attribute `Data`, step 4 routes that raw OCTETS value into the generic parser, steps 5-7 reinterpret the `0x`-prefixed bytes as a 34-byte base16 input whose fifth pair is `0x20 0xff`, and step 8 forwards `p[1] == 0xff` to step 9, where it becomes index 255 into the 255-byte decode table.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 reproduced the saved crash with `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42502974 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which ran `/out/fuzzer_tacacs` on the staged `poc` and produced the ASan global-buffer-overflow in `fr_is_base16_nstd`.

format.name: TACACS+ authorization response packet
format.contract: The trigger witness is exactly the saved 80-byte `poc`. Its trigger-critical structure is an unencrypted TACACS authorization-response packet whose body has `arg_cnt=9`, arg lengths `[0,2,0,0,0,0,0,0,41]`, and a final 41-byte argument `DATa*0x` + 9x`0x20` + `0xff 0xff` + 23x`0x20`. The mixed-case name must resolve case-insensitively to TACACS attribute `Data`, and the nine-space alignment after the literal `0x` must be preserved so the 34-byte would-be hex payload reaches a fifth decode pair `0x20 0xff` and the crash occurs on that pair's second byte `0xff`.
